# Upgrade handoff: SSL configuration, 0.28.0 → 0.28.1

This note is for contributors. It covers the one SSL change between HTTPX 0.28.0 and 0.28.1, what it means for users, and where the SSL guidance in the docs does not match the 0.28.1 source.

## Evidence and scope

| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Repository | `encode/httpx` |
| Before revision | `80960fa31918d7663c3f4c3ad61661cf0e80628f` |
| After revision (this tree) | `26d48e0634e6ee9cdc0533996db289ce4b430177`. `httpx/__version__.py` reports `0.28.1` |
| Fix commit | [`89599a9541af14bcf906fc4ed58ccbdf403802ba`](https://github.com/encode/httpx/commit/89599a9541af14bcf906fc4ed58ccbdf403802ba), 2024-12-04, parent `8ecb86f0d74ffc52d4663214fae9526bee89358d` |
| Before-tag file supplied | [`httpx/_config.py` @ `80960fa`](https://github.com/encode/httpx/blob/80960fa31918d7663c3f4c3ad61661cf0e80628f/httpx/_config.py) (git blob `dbd2b46cd1`) |

Limits of this review:

- The evidence includes only one file from before the tag (`httpx/_config.py`) and the diff for the fix commit. Nothing here shows whether other files changed between `80960fa` and `26d48e0`. The one exception is `CHANGELOG.md`: the fix commit added the entry under `## Dev`, and in this tree it sits under `## 0.28.1 (6th December, 2024)`, so a separate release commit must have renamed the heading.
- I compared the before and after copies of `httpx/_config.py` line by line. They differ only in the hunk shown in the fix diff. `Timeout`, `Limits`, `Proxy` and the defaults are the same.
- Everything in this note comes from reading the source. I did not run any code or tests. Statements about standard-library `ssl` behaviour are marked as inferences.

## What changed

The only code change is in `create_ssl_context()`, in the `verify is False` branch (`httpx/_config.py:41-44`).

Before (0.28.0):

```python
elif verify is False:
    ssl_context = ssl.SSLContext(ssl.PROTOCOL_TLS_CLIENT)
    ssl_context.check_hostname = False
    ssl_context.verify_mode = ssl.CERT_NONE
    return ssl_context
```

After (0.28.1):

```python
elif verify is False:
    ctx = ssl.SSLContext(ssl.PROTOCOL_TLS_CLIENT)
    ctx.check_hostname = False
    ctx.verify_mode = ssl.CERT_NONE
```

In 0.28.0 the early `return` meant that `verify=False` never reached the `if cert:` block (`httpx/_config.py:58-67`). Any `cert=...` argument was **silently ignored**: no certificate chain was loaded and no deprecation warning was raised. In 0.28.1 this branch falls through to the shared `cert` handling, the same way `verify=True` and `verify=<SSLContext>` already did.

The changelog entry is in `CHANGELOG.md:7-9`: "Fix SSL case where `verify=False` together with client side certificates."

`create_ssl_context()` is called from `HTTPTransport.__init__` (`httpx/_transports/default.py:153`) and `AsyncHTTPTransport.__init__` (`httpx/_transports/default.py:297`). `Client` and `AsyncClient` pass `verify`/`cert`/`trust_env` through to those transports (`httpx/_client.py:690`, `:703`, `:733`, `:752` and the async equivalents at `:1404`, `:1418`, `:1447`, `:1466`). The fix therefore applies to the top-level API, both clients and both transports.

## Behaviour matrix for `create_ssl_context(verify, cert, trust_env)`

| `verify` | `cert` | 0.28.0 | 0.28.1 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `True` | `None` | Default context (certifi, or `SSL_CERT_FILE`/`SSL_CERT_DIR` if `trust_env`) | Unchanged |
| `True` | set | Cert loaded, `DeprecationWarning` | Unchanged |
| `False` | `None` | `CERT_NONE`, no hostname check | Unchanged |
| `False` | set | **Cert ignored, no warning** | **Cert loaded, `DeprecationWarning`** |
| `SSLContext` | `None` | Context used as-is | Unchanged |
| `SSLContext` | set | Cert loaded into the caller's context, `DeprecationWarning` | Unchanged |
| `str` (path) | `None` | `DeprecationWarning`, context from cafile/capath | Unchanged |
| `str` (path) | set | `verify` warning only. **Cert ignored** | **Still ignored** (see below) |

## Upgrade impact

For users who pass `verify=False` together with `cert=...`:

1. **The client certificate is now actually presented.** Servers that require mutual TLS and rejected these clients under 0.28.0 should now accept them. This is the intended fix.
2. **A `DeprecationWarning` is now raised** (`httpx/_config.py:59-63`). Test suites that turn warnings into errors will start failing where they did not before. HTTPX's own suite does this (`pyproject.toml:119-120`, `filterwarnings = ["error", ...]`).
3. **Bad certificate paths now fail when the transport is built.** *(Inference from standard-library behaviour.)* `SSLContext.load_cert_chain()` raises on a missing file or a bad key, and a wrong path was previously never read. Configurations that only "worked" because the cert was dropped will now raise when `Client`/`HTTPTransport` is constructed.

Nothing changes for users who don't combine `verify=False` with `cert`.

### Recommended non-deprecated equivalent

`cert=` is deprecated as of 0.28.0 (`CHANGELOG.md:21-22`). The equivalent setup that doesn't trigger the warning, built the same way the source builds it (`httpx/_config.py:42-44`, `:64-67`):

```python
import ssl
import httpx

ctx = ssl.SSLContext(ssl.PROTOCOL_TLS_CLIENT)
ctx.check_hostname = False          # must be cleared before CERT_NONE
ctx.verify_mode = ssl.CERT_NONE
ctx.load_cert_chain(certfile="path/to/client.pem")  # optionally keyfile / password
client = httpx.Client(verify=ctx)
```

### Edge case still open: `verify=<str>` with `cert`

The deprecated string branch still returns early (`httpx/_config.py:45-54`), before the `cert` block. `verify="path/to/ca.pem", cert="client.pem"` therefore still drops the client certificate without any warning about the drop. Only the `verify=<str>` deprecation warning appears. This is the same kind of bug the 0.28.1 fix addressed for `verify=False`, and the fix commit doesn't touch it. Contributors should decide whether to fix it the same way or leave it until both deprecated paths are removed.

## Docs/source consistency

Findings are in priority order. None of these documentation files are in the fix diff. Each one is a finding about the 0.28.1 tree; none was introduced by the upgrade.

1. **`docs/advanced/ssl.md` doesn't cover a client certificate with verification disabled.** The "Client side certificates" section (`docs/advanced/ssl.md:60-70`) only shows `ssl.create_default_context()` plus `load_cert_chain()`. The "Enabling and disabling verification" section (`:12-17`) only shows bare `verify=False`. Users following the guidance to drop `cert=` have no documented route for the exact case 0.28.1 fixed. Suggested fix: add the snippet from "Recommended non-deprecated equivalent" above.
2. **The docs say `SSL_CERT_FILE`/`SSL_CERT_DIR` are not read automatically, but the source reads them.** `docs/advanced/ssl.md:74` says HTTPX "does not automatically pull in the environment variables `SSL_CERT_FILE` or `SSL_CERT_DIR`". `httpx/_config.py:33-37` uses them when `verify is True` and `trust_env` is true, which is the default for both `Client` and the transports. Details the docs also miss:
   - `SSL_CERT_FILE` takes priority and `SSL_CERT_DIR` is only used when it is unset. The doc example (`docs/advanced/ssl.md:81-84`) passes both at once.
   - Neither variable is used when `verify=False` or `verify=<SSLContext>`.
   - `docs/environment_variables.md` lists only proxy variables, although the test fixture treats both SSL variables as environment-sensitive (`tests/conftest.py:23-31`).

   The before-tag `_config.py` has the same env-var logic (lines 33-40), so this mismatch already existed in 0.28.0.
3. **`docs/logging.md:23-24` shows httpx debug lines that the source no longer produces.** The example output includes `httpx - load_ssl_context verify=True cert=None` and `httpx - load_verify_locations cafile=...`. No `httpx` module emits these. The only `logger.` calls are the `INFO` request lines at `httpx/_client.py:1025` and `:1740`. Readers debugging SSL setup will look for log lines that never appear.
4. **Docstrings are consistent.** `verify` is documented as `True`, `False` or `ssl.SSLContext` in `httpx/_api.py:85-87` and `httpx/_client.py:617-619` / `:1331-1333`, and `cert` is deliberately left undocumented. This matches the 0.28 deprecation stance, and no change is needed.
5. **Minor nits** (low priority, optional):
   - The `cert` deprecation message is built from two adjacent string literals with no space between them, so it renders as "...instead,with `.load_cert_chain()`..." (`httpx/_config.py:60-61`).
   - Typos in `docs/advanced/ssl.md`: "equivelent" (`:32`) and "Loding" (`:49`).
   - The env-var example at `docs/advanced/ssl.md:78-86` uses `os` and `certifi` without importing them.

## Test coverage

- The `if cert:` block is marked `# pragma: nocover` (`httpx/_config.py:58`), and no test passes `cert=` to `create_ssl_context`, `Client` or a transport. **The 0.28.1 fix has no regression test.**
- `tests/test_config.py:76-79` checks only `verify_mode == CERT_NONE` and `check_hostname is False` for `verify=False`. Under 0.28.0 that test passed and still missed the bug.
- A regression test would call `create_ssl_context(verify=False, cert=(cert_pem_file, cert_private_key_file))` inside `pytest.warns(DeprecationWarning)`, using the existing `trustme` fixtures (`tests/conftest.py:186-212`). It would then assert that the context still has `CERT_NONE` and that the cert was loaded. Because of `filterwarnings = error`, the `pytest.warns` wrapper is required. I have not written or run this test.

## Suggested follow-ups (not done here)

1. Add the regression test described above.
2. Add the "client certificate with verification disabled" example to `docs/advanced/ssl.md`.
3. Correct the `SSL_CERT_FILE`/`SSL_CERT_DIR` statement in `docs/advanced/ssl.md`, and consider documenting both variables in `docs/environment_variables.md`.
4. Refresh or trim the sample output in `docs/logging.md`.
5. Decide what to do about `verify=<str>` together with `cert`.

## How this note was checked

- Compared `../evidence/before/httpx/_config.py` with `httpx/_config.py` line by line. The only difference is the `verify is False` hunk in `../evidence/fix.diff`.
- Checked that the `CHANGELOG.md` text in the fix diff appears in this tree under the 0.28.1 heading.
- Searched (Grep) for every use of `create_ssl_context`, `cert`, `verify`, `SSL_CERT_FILE`/`SSL_CERT_DIR` and `logger.` across `httpx/`, `docs/` and `tests/`. Every file:line reference above comes from those reads.
- I did not run code, tests, or anything over the network.

# Upgrade handoff: SSL configuration, 0.28.0 → 0.28.1

For contributors picking up SSL configuration work after the 0.28.1 fix. It covers
what changed in `create_ssl_context()`, who is affected, and where the SSL guidance
in the docs, docstrings and tests does not match the source.

## Evidence and limits

| Item | Reference |
| --- | --- |
| Before revision (0.28.0, per task) | [`80960fa`](https://github.com/encode/httpx/tree/80960fa31918d7663c3f4c3ad61661cf0e80628f): [`httpx/_config.py`](https://github.com/encode/httpx/blob/80960fa31918d7663c3f4c3ad61661cf0e80628f/httpx/_config.py) (blob `dbd2b46`) |
| Fix commit | [`89599a9`](https://github.com/encode/httpx/commit/89599a9541af14bcf906fc4ed58ccbdf403802ba), 2024-12-04; changes only `CHANGELOG.md` and `httpx/_config.py` |
| After revision (this tree) | [`26d48e0`](https://github.com/encode/httpx/tree/26d48e0634e6ee9cdc0533996db289ce4b430177); `httpx/__version__.py` reads `0.28.1` |

Everything below comes from reading the source. Nothing was run: no tests, no
code and no TLS connections. The fix diff's pre-image blob ID matches the supplied
before file. The post-image matches [`httpx/_config.py`](../httpx/_config.py) lines
41–44 in this tree. For the before revision, only `httpx/_config.py` was supplied,
so this handoff does not say how other before-tag files, including the SSL docs,
read at 0.28.0. The release date (6 December 2024) comes from
[`CHANGELOG.md`](../CHANGELOG.md) and was not checked against the package index.

## What changed

In 0.28.0, the `verify is False` branch of `create_ssl_context()` built a
non-verifying context and **returned it immediately**, so the code never reached the
`cert` handling below it. 0.28.1 assigns that context to `ctx` and falls through
instead. The changelog describes this as "Fix SSL case where `verify=False` together
with client side certificates."

Current flow in [`httpx/_config.py`](../httpx/_config.py) (lines 23–69):

| `verify` | Context | Does `cert=` reach `load_cert_chain()`? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `True` | `SSL_CERT_FILE`, else `SSL_CERT_DIR` when `trust_env` is true, otherwise certifi | Yes |
| `False` | `SSLContext(PROTOCOL_TLS_CLIENT)` with `check_hostname=False`, `CERT_NONE` | **Yes since 0.28.1**. In 0.28.0 `cert` was silently ignored |
| `str` (deprecated) | `create_default_context(cafile=/capath=)` | **No**: returns early (lines 52–54), see [findings](#guidance-and-source-consistency) |
| `ssl.SSLContext` | The caller's context, used as is | Yes, and it mutates that object |

Whenever `cert` is used, it emits a `DeprecationWarning` that recommends
`verify=<ssl_context>` with `.load_cert_chain()`. `Client`, `AsyncClient` and the
proxy transports pass `verify`, `cert` and `trust_env` to `HTTPTransport` and
`AsyncHTTPTransport`, which call `create_ssl_context()`
([`httpx/_client.py`](../httpx/_client.py) lines 688–758,
[`httpx/_transports/default.py`](../httpx/_transports/default.py) lines 153 and 297).

### Effect on callers using `verify=False, cert=...`

From the code path, not from runs:

- Since 0.28.1 the client certificate is loaded and offered. Before, it was dropped
  without any message.
- These callers now get the `cert=` `DeprecationWarning`. Test suites that treat
  warnings as errors may fail on it.
- Errors from `load_cert_chain()` now surface where they were hidden before, such as
  a missing key file. `tests/test_config.py` lines 70–73 expect `ssl.SSLError` for a
  certificate without a key.

The supported path, according to `CHANGELOG.md` 0.28.0 and
[`docs/advanced/ssl.md`](advanced/ssl.md#client-side-certificates), is to build an
`ssl.SSLContext`, call `.load_cert_chain()` on it and pass it as `verify=`.

## Guidance and source consistency

These conflicts are still open in this tree. None is decided by the 0.28.1 fix, and
each fix listed below is a proposal, not a decision.

1. **`SSL_CERT_FILE`/`SSL_CERT_DIR` are read by default, but the docs say they are
   not.** [`docs/advanced/ssl.md`](advanced/ssl.md#working-with-ssl_cert_file-and-ssl_cert_dir)
   line 74 says httpx "does not automatically pull in" these variables and that they
   must be enabled explicitly. `create_ssl_context()` reads them when `verify=True`
   and `trust_env=True` (`_config.py` lines 34–37), and both are the defaults. The
   before-tag `_config.py` has the same branch, so the 0.28.1 fix did not cause this.
   [`docs/environment_variables.md`](environment_variables.md) lists only the proxy
   variables. The intended behaviour has not been decided: either the code or the docs
   should change. `tests/conftest.py` clears both variables for every test, and no
   test in the inspected `tests/` sets them.
2. **`verify=<str>` still ignores `cert`.** That branch returns before the `cert`
   block, so a call like `verify="ca.pem", cert=...` drops the certificate with no
   `cert` deprecation warning. This is the same kind of bug that 0.28.1 fixed for
   `verify=False`. Both arguments are deprecated, so a maintainer needs to decide
   whether a fix is wanted.
3. **No regression test covers the fix.** `tests/test_config.py::test_load_ssl_config_no_verify`
   (line 76) calls `create_ssl_context(verify=False)` without `cert`. No `cert=`
   argument appears anywhere in `tests/`, and the `cert` block is marked
   `# pragma: nocover`.
4. **The `verify=False` client-certificate case has no documented replacement.**
   `docs/advanced/ssl.md` shows `.load_cert_chain()` only on a verifying
   `create_default_context()`. Users moving off `cert=` while keeping
   `verify=False` have no documented example. One possible fix (proposed): add an
   example that builds the non-verifying context the way `_config.py` lines 42–44 do
   and then calls `.load_cert_chain()`.
5. **The logging example looks stale.** [`docs/logging.md`](logging.md) lines 23–24
   show `httpx - load_ssl_context ...` and `httpx - load_verify_locations ...` debug
   lines. Searching `httpx/` turns up no matching log call. The only `logger.` calls
   are the request `info` lines in `_client.py` (lines 1025 and 1740). The example
   is dated 2024-09-28.
6. **The docstrings omit the deprecated forms.** The `verify` docstrings in
   `_client.py` (lines 617 and 1331) and `_api.py` (line 85) describe only `True`,
   `False` and an `SSLContext`, but the signatures also accept `str`. The
   `Client`/`AsyncClient` signatures also accept `cert`, which has no docstring entry.
   The top-level `_api.py` functions take no `cert` argument. Leaving the deprecated
   forms out of the docstrings may be intentional. Nothing in the inspected material
   says whether it is.

## Next checks

- Ask a maintainer to decide finding 1 before editing either `ssl.md` or the
  `trust_env` branch.
- Run the existing suite and a `verify=False, cert=...` regression test in a real
  environment. This handoff ran neither.

The before-tag file is the only 14.1.0 file supplied. The fix diff covers one
commit, not the full 14.1.0..14.1.1 range. The evidence bundle records SHA-256
values for the before-tag file and the diff. They were not recomputed in this
review.

## Matching behavior: inner-literal fix (BUG #2884)

**Reported upstream (CHANGELOG):** 14.1.0 could miss lines that should match
(false negatives). The reported example is `(?i:e.x|ex)`, which did not match
`e-x`. The CHANGELOG places the bug in the `grep-regex` inner-literal
optimization, not in the `regex` crate, and says the affected set of regexes is
hard to characterize.

**Code change (observed in the before file, the fix diff and this tree):** the
fix touches only `crates/regex/src/literal.rs` (crate `grep-regex`, version
0.1.13 in this tree):

- `Extractor::union` now ends with `seq1.prefix = seq1.prefix && seq2.prefix`
  ([literal.rs:433](crates/regex/src/literal.rs#L433)). Before, the union kept
  only `seq1`'s prefix tag. `cross` uses that tag to decide whether to cross a
  sequence forward or fall back to `choose`
  ([literal.rs:384-398](crates/regex/src/literal.rs#L384-L398)).
- `TSeq::choose` now marks both candidate sequences inexact before choosing one
  ([literal.rs:592-597](crates/regex/src/literal.rs#L592-L597)). The code
  comment gives the rationale: choosing one sequence discards the other.

**Where this applies (code):** these literals build `fast_line_regex`
([matcher.rs:78](crates/regex/src/matcher.rs#L78)), which
`find_candidate_line` uses to report candidate lines
([matcher.rs:491-506](crates/regex/src/matcher.rs#L491-L506)). The field's
comment says this regex "never reports false negatives"
([matcher.rs:373-377](crates/regex/src/matcher.rs#L373-L377)), and #2884
violated that. `InnerLiterals::new` skips extraction in these cases
([literal.rs:55-93](crates/regex/src/literal.rs#L55-L93)):

- no line terminator is configured;
- the regex engine reports acceleration and the pattern has no Unicode word
  boundary;
- the pattern is an alternation of literals.

The fix diff does not touch the PCRE2 matcher in `crates/pcre2`.

**Changed unit-test expectations (`literal.rs` tests, from the fix diff):**

| Pattern | 14.1.0 expectation | 14.1.1 expectation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `[a-z]([a-z]foo)(bar[a-z])[a-z]` | `I("foobar")` | `I("foo")` |
| `[a-z]([a-z]foo){3}(bar[a-z]){3}[a-z]` | `I("foobar")` | `I("foo")` |
| `[A-Z]+123` | `E("123")` | `I("123")` |
| `1\|[A-Z]2\|3` | `E("1"), E("2"), E("3")` | `E("1"), I("2"), E("3")` |
| `(?:\|1)[A-Z]2` | `E("2")` | `I("2")` |
| `(?i:e.x\|ex)` (new test `case_insensitive_alternation`) | — | `I("X"), I("x")` |

`E` = exact literal and `I` = inexact literal (test helpers in `literal.rs`).

**Implications for contributors:**

- Code or tests that depend on extracted inner literals should expect the 14.1.1
  values above. For some patterns, the 14.1.1 literals are shorter or inexact.
- These patterns may now use a less selective prefilter. That performance effect
  is an inference from the code change. It was not benchmarked.
- No integration test in `tests/` references #2884 or `e-x`. Coverage is the
  `literal.rs` unit test above.
- **Unknown:** this review did not trace how the old exactness or prefix tags
  caused a dropped match through `regex-syntax`'s `Seq` operations, such as
  `optimize_for_prefix_by_preference` in `extract_untagged`. The CHANGELOG
  statement is the only source for the end-to-end false negative.

**Test harness change in the same commit:** `TestCommand::stdout` and
`TestCommand::pipe` in `tests/util.rs` now return
`String::from_utf8_lossy(..).into_owned()` instead of using `parse()` with a
panic message ([tests/util.rs:287](tests/util.rs#L287),
[tests/util.rs:307](tests/util.rs#L307)). This affects only integration-test
helpers.

## Build-feature compatibility

**Reported upstream:** the CHANGELOG lists MISC #2748, "Remove ripgrep's
`simd-accel` feature because it was frequently broken." The README note under
[Building](README.md#building) says that the feature required a nightly
compiler, benefited only UTF-16 transcoding and has been removed.

**Observed in this tree (14.1.1):**

- The root `ripgrep` package declares one feature, `pcre2 = ["grep/pcre2"]`
  ([Cargo.toml:70-71](Cargo.toml#L70-L71)). Deb packaging enables it
  ([Cargo.toml:96](Cargo.toml#L96)). The package declares
  `rust-version = "1.72"` ([Cargo.toml:27](Cargo.toml#L27)).
- Library crates still declare `simd-accel = []` and mark it deprecated:
  - `grep` and `grep-searcher` also declare `avx-accel = []`, with the comment
    "Runtime dispatch is used for SIMD now"
    ([crates/grep/Cargo.toml:31-33](crates/grep/Cargo.toml#L31-L33),
    [crates/searcher/Cargo.toml:30-32](crates/searcher/Cargo.toml#L30-L32)).
  - `globset` and `ignore` call it "DEPRECATED. It is a no-op"
    ([crates/globset/Cargo.toml:44-46](crates/globset/Cargo.toml#L44-L46),
    [crates/ignore/Cargo.toml:42-44](crates/ignore/Cargo.toml#L42-L44)).

**Implications for contributors and packagers:**

- If a build passes `--features simd-accel` to the `ripgrep` package, it names a
  feature that the 14.1.1 manifest does not declare. Remove the flag. This
  review did not run Cargo to observe the resulting error.
- Downstream crates that enable `simd-accel` or `avx-accel` on `grep`,
  `grep-searcher`, `globset` or `ignore` still match declared features. The
  manifests describe those features as deprecated no-ops.
- **Unknown:** the 14.1.0 `Cargo.toml` files were not supplied. The previous
  root feature list, the `pcre2` feature definition and the MSRV have not been
  compared with 14.1.0. The CHANGELOG lists no other build-feature change for
  14.1.1.

## Related documentation observation

At the after tag, the README's Debian install example still downloads
`ripgrep_14.1.0-1_amd64.deb` ([README.md:339-340](README.md#L339-L340)). The
README was not edited in this review except to add a link to this file.

- `cargo test -p grep-regex`: confirm the updated `literal.rs` expectations.
- `cargo test --all`: run the full suite from the README.
- Compare `rg '(?i:e.x|ex)'` on input containing `e-x` across a 14.1.0 build

sessions.final_message:
I wrote `UPGRADE-HANDOFF.md` and added one link to it at the end of `README.md`. I only read the source; nothing was built, run or tested.

**What the handoff covers**
- **Missed matches fixed (BUG #2884):** in 14.1.0, ripgrep could skip lines that should match (for example, `(?i:e.x|ex)` didn't match `e-x`). The bug was in ripgrep's own shortcut that looks for fixed strings before running the full regex. The fix is two small changes in `crates/regex/src/literal.rs` (lines 433 and 596–597). The handoff explains which searches use that shortcut: those with `-U/--multiline` don't, and neither does PCRE2. Upgrading can only add matching lines, never remove them, though which strings the shortcut picks may change, so some searches may run faster or slower. It also has a table of the six unit-test expectations that changed.
- **`simd-accel` removed:** in this release the top-level `ripgrep` package offers only the `pcre2` build feature, so build scripts that ask for `--features simd-accel` should drop it. I didn't run Cargo to confirm it rejects that. The `grep`, `grep-searcher`, `ignore` and `globset` libraries still accept `simd-accel`, but it does nothing.
- **Test helper cleanup:** `stdout()` and `pipe()` in `tests/util.rs` were simplified; their behavior is unchanged.
- **Checklist:** commands for contributors to run themselves, clearly marked as not run by me.

**Checks**
- **README:** the original 524 lines are unchanged. I made a single edit after the last line, adding a blank line and the link (lines 525–526).
- **`literal.rs` comparison:** I compared the 14.1.0 file with the 14.1.1 file line by line. Apart from the fix, the only difference is a typo fixed in a comment ("underyling" → "underlying" on line 18). That's why its fingerprint doesn't match the "before" side of the fix diff.
- **Line references:** I checked each cited line range against the files.

**Limits of the evidence**
The only 14.1.0 file supplied was `literal.rs`. So the claim that `simd-accel` existed in 14.1.0 and was removed comes from the 14.1.1 CHANGELOG and README, not from the old `Cargo.toml`; the handoff says so. Separately, the README's Debian install example still points to the 14.1.0 package. The handoff mentions this but I didn't change it.

I didn't modify any other files or the evidence, and I didn't use the network, run code or create other files.
sessions.handoff:
Contributor upgrade handoff: ripgrep 14.1.0 → 14.1.1
====================================================
Scope: matching behavior and build-feature compatibility. This handoff was
prepared by source inspection only. Nothing was compiled, executed or tested
while writing it.

### Evidence

| Item | Value |
| ---- | ----- |
| Before revision (14.1.0) | `e50df40a1967708b9781486b1c017e48040bceb0` |
| After revision (14.1.1) | `4649aa9700619f94cf9c66876e9549d83420e16c` (this tree) |
| Fix commit | [`9d738ad0c009e6632d75fa3d36051e5ae7f7cce6`](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/commit/9d738ad0c009e6632d75fa3d36051e5ae7f7cce6) (2024-09-09, parent `6c5108ed1798…`) |
| Before-tag file supplied | [`crates/regex/src/literal.rs` @ `e50df40`](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/blob/e50df40a1967708b9781486b1c017e48040bceb0/crates/regex/src/literal.rs) (git blob `e2f158b6…`) |
| Release notes | [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md), section `14.1.1 (2024-09-08)` |

The only before-tag file supplied is `literal.rs`. The fix diff touches
`crates/regex/src/literal.rs` and `tests/util.rs`. All other "before"
statements below rely on the after-tree CHANGELOG and README, and say so.

The pre-image blob in the fix diff (`a45f749e29`) differs from the 14.1.0 blob
(`e2f158b6…`). Comparing the 14.1.0 file with this tree shows one extra change
outside the fix: a doc-comment typo on line 18 (`underyling` → `underlying`).
Apart from that, every 14.1.0 → 14.1.1 change in `literal.rs` comes from the
fix diff.

### 1. Matching behavior: false negatives fixed (BUG #2884)

**What users saw.** In 14.1.0, ripgrep could skip lines that should match.
The CHANGELOG's reported example is that `(?i:e.x|ex)` did not match `e-x`.
The CHANGELOG also says the bug was in ripgrep's own inner-literal optimization
in `grep-regex`, not in the `regex` crate.

**Where it lives.** `InnerLiterals` (`crates/regex/src/literal.rs:41-124`)
extracts literals from the pattern, and `RegexMatcher` compiles them into
`fast_line_regex` (`crates/regex/src/matcher.rs:78`). That regex drives
`find_candidate_line` (`crates/regex/src/matcher.rs:491-506`). The trait
contract allows false positives but no false negatives
(`crates/matcher/src/lib.rs:1112-1114`). Bad literals broke that contract.
When the candidate regex missed a matching line, the full regex never saw
that line.

**What changed** (two hunks in `crates/regex/src/literal.rs`):

1. `TSeq::choose` (`literal.rs:592-629`) now calls `make_inexact()` on both
   inputs before it picks one. Choosing one sequence means the other is
   dropped, so the result cannot be exact.
2. `Extractor::union` (`literal.rs:403-435`) now sets
   `seq1.prefix = seq1.prefix && seq2.prefix` (line 433). Before, a "not a
   prefix" tag from a concatenation branch was lost when that branch was
   unioned into an alternation.

**When the code path is used** (anything outside these conditions is not
affected):

- A line terminator must be configured (`literal.rs:58-64`). Normal ripgrep
  searches set `\n`, or NUL with `--null-data`
  (`crates/core/flags/hiargs.rs:482-494`). With `-U/--multiline`, ripgrep does
  not set one, and `--crlf` explicitly clears it (`hiargs.rs:477-481`). The
  default is `None` (`crates/regex/src/config.rs:61`).
- The pattern must not already be accelerated by the regex engine, unless it
  contains Unicode word boundaries (`literal.rs:73-81`).
- The pattern must not be a plain alternation of literals
  (`literal.rs:84-90`).
- Only the Rust regex engine is affected, which is the default and the primary
  engine for `--engine auto`. The PCRE2 matcher (`crates/pcre2`) does not use
  this module.

**Expected user-visible effect.** On 14.1.1, some line-oriented searches report
lines that 14.1.0 missed. No pattern should report fewer matching lines because
of this fix: the change only makes literal sequences less exact or marks them
as non-prefix. Candidate-literal selection can also change, which may affect
throughput. Treat this as a possible performance change, not a correctness
change.

**Test expectation changes** (`literal.rs` unit tests, from the fix diff):

| Pattern | 14.1.0 expected | 14.1.1 expected |
| ------- | --------------- | --------------- |
| `[a-z]([a-z]foo)(bar[a-z])[a-z]` | `I("foobar")` | `I("foo")` |
| `[a-z]([a-z]foo){3}(bar[a-z]){3}[a-z]` | `I("foobar")` | `I("foo")` |
| `[A-Z]+123` | `E("123")` | `I("123")` |
| `1\|[A-Z]2\|3` | `E("1"), E("2"), E("3")` | `E("1"), I("2"), E("3")` |
| `(?:\|1)[A-Z]2` | `E("2")` | `I("2")` |
| `(?i:e.x\|ex)` (new, `case_insensitive_alternation`) | none | `I("X"), I("x")` |

(`E` = exact, `I` = inexact. The new regression test is at
`literal.rs:1015-1020`.) If you add extractor tests, remember that literals
that survive a `choose` are now always inexact.

### 2. Build-feature compatibility: `simd-accel` removed from `ripgrep`

**Source:** CHANGELOG 14.1.1, MISC #2748: "Remove ripgrep's `simd-accel`
feature because it was frequently broken." See also the README "Building"
note. The 14.1.0 `Cargo.toml` was not supplied, so the evidence does not
directly show the before state of the manifest.

**State of this tree:**

- The root `ripgrep` package declares one feature, `pcre2 = ["grep/pcre2"]`
  (`Cargo.toml:70-71`). With 14.1.1, Cargo should reject a build that asks for
  `--features simd-accel` on the `ripgrep` package. Remove it from build
  scripts, packaging recipes and CI. (This was not confirmed by running Cargo.)
- The library crates still declare `simd-accel` as a deprecated no-op, so
  downstream manifests that enable it still resolve:
  - `grep` 0.3.2: `crates/grep/Cargo.toml:31-33` (`simd-accel`, `avx-accel`)
  - `grep-searcher` 0.1.14: `crates/searcher/Cargo.toml:30-32` (`simd-accel`, `avx-accel`)
  - `ignore` 0.4.23: `crates/ignore/Cargo.toml:42-44`
  - `globset` 0.4.15: `crates/globset/Cargo.toml:44-46`
- The repo's CI and release scripts only pass `--features pcre2`
  (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:147,165`, `.github/workflows/release.yml:177`,
  `ci/build-and-publish-m2:25`). Nothing in the tree still asks for
  `simd-accel` on the binary.
- PCRE2 builds are unchanged: `--features pcre2` works as before. The Debian
  package metadata still enables it (`Cargo.toml:96`).
- The MSRV at the after revision is Rust 1.72 (`Cargo.toml:27`, README
  "Building"). The evidence does not show any MSRV change in this release.
- SIMD for UTF-16 transcoding (the only thing `simd-accel` affected) is not
  available in this release. The README directs anyone who needs it to
  `encoding_rs`.

### 3. Test-harness cleanup (no behavior change)

`tests/util.rs` `TestCommand::stdout` and `TestCommand::pipe`
(`tests/util.rs:285-288`, `291-308`) now return
`String::from_utf8_lossy(..).into_owned()` instead of going through
`str::parse` with an unreachable panic arm. Both still return `String`.
Integration tests that call these helpers do not need changes.

### Contributor checklist

None of these were run while writing this handoff:

- [ ] `cargo test -p grep-regex case_insensitive_alternation` (regression
      test for #2884).
- [ ] `cargo test -p grep-regex` (picks up the updated `various` and
      `anything` expectations).
- [ ] End to end: `printf 'e-x\n' | rg '(?i:e.x|ex)'` should print `e-x` on
      14.1.1.
- [ ] Search build and packaging configs outside this repo for
      `--features simd-accel` (or `features = ["simd-accel"]`) on the
      `ripgrep` package, and drop it. Library-crate uses can stay for now
      because they are no-ops.
- [ ] `cargo build --release --features pcre2` still builds.

### Out of scope / not evidenced

- 14.1.0 versions of `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock`, crate manifests and
  `tests/util.rs` were not supplied. Version bumps between the tags and the
  commit that removed `simd-accel` are not evidenced beyond the CHANGELOG.
- The README `.deb` install example still refers to `14.1.0` at the after
  revision. This handoff does not change that.
